purpose: Reorder a controlled vertical list using pointer dragging, keyboard dragging or explicit move actions.
behaviorProvider: dnd-kit core/sortable sensors and collision strategy, plus shared IconButton controls.

host: stable unique IDs and accepted order

requirements.statement: Reject empty or duplicate string IDs. Use IDs as React keys and sortable identities independently of display labels.
Render items in the supplied order and emit an ordered ID array with activeId, overId and drag or move-button source. Do not mutate the input array or keep a second accepted order.

Use PointerSensor and KeyboardSensor with sortableKeyboardCoordinates, a vertical list strategy and closest-center collision detection. Bind sensor listeners and attributes to the actual named drag-handle button.
Provide drag instructions and live announcements for pick-up, target position and finish/cancel. Space starts and drops keyboard dragging; Escape cancels through dnd-kit.
Provide named up/down IconButtons that emit adjacent moves. Disable up for the first item, down for the last item, and all reordering controls when disabled.
Do not emit a reorder for a cancelled drag, missing drop target, same active/over ID or disabled list.
Snapshot IDs/order on drag start. If the supplied order changed by drag end, decline the move and announce that no move was applied.
Accept emitted ID order by reordering the same stable records and persist separately. Keep IDs stable across renames; reject unauthorized changes and resolve concurrent server updates in the host.
Give the list a useful name and each item a descriptive label even with renderItem. Custom interactive content must remain usable outside the dedicated drag handle.
Use data-display group tokens for list/item layout and preserve nested IconButton trigger ownership. Drag transforms are measured runtime coordinates, not fixed design values.

limitations: One vertical list only; no cross-list transfer, nested tree, virtualization or multi-select dragging.
There is no optimistic persisted state or server synchronization. Explicit move announcements describe a requested move, which the host may reject.
Rows intentionally have no animated reorder transition; the host should verify unusually tall or complex custom items.
